GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUSTION No. 2992 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 15.03.2021 
  
ST STATUS FOR COMMUNITIES 
 
2992. SHRI GAURAV GOGOI: 
SHRI ABDUL KHALEQUE: 
  
 Will the Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether the Government has received the State Government of Assam’s report on the 
granting of Scheduled Tribe (ST) status to six communities, namely Chutiya, Koch-Rajbongshi, 
Motok, Moran, Tai-Ahom and Tea Tribe in Assam; 
  
(b) if so, the timeline for implementation of such reservation; 
  
(c) whether the Government has information regarding the details of all the committees formed 
in the matter since 2015; and 
  
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE FOR TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
(SMT. RENUKA SINGH SARUTA) 
  
(a) & (b) : Yes Sir, proposal has been received from the State Government of Assam for 
inclusion/granting of Scheduled Tribes(ST) status to six communities, namely Matak, Maran, 
Tai Ahom, Chutia and Koch Rajbongshi and Tea Tribes in Assam. The Government of India on 
15.6.1999 (further amended on 25.6.2002), has laid down the modalities for determining the 
claims for inclusion in, exclusion from and other modification in the Orders specifying list of 
Scheduled Tribes. According to these modalities, only those proposals which have been 
recommended and justified by the concerned State Government/Union Territory Administration 
and concurred with by the Registrar General of India(RGI) and the National Commission for 
Scheduled Tribes are to be considered for amendment of legislation. All actions are taken with 
respect to proposals of State/UT Governments for the communities demanding Scheduled 
Tribes status as per these modalities. As such, no timeline can be specified for inclusion of 
communities. 
  
(c) & (d) :  A Committee was constituted vide Ministry of Home Affairs (NE-Division) Order No. 
11012/43/2016-NE-IV dated 29th February, 2016 to recommend the modalities for granting of 
Scheduled Tribes status to six Communities namely, Koch Rajbongshi, Moran, Matak, Tai 
Ahom, Chutia and Adivasi (Tea Tribes) in Assam under the chairmanship of Special Secretary 
(IS), Ministry of Home Affairs with its members- Registrar General of India, Joint Secretary of 
Ministry of Tribal Affairs, Joint Secretary (NE), GoI’s representative for peace talks (Special 
invitees),  Director (NE)( Member Secretary).The Committee also included representatives of 
Govt. of Assam. 
    As per the order, the Committee was required to suggest the modalities for the required 
reservations, of shifting the existing reservation for these communities from OBC to ST, 
protecting the interests of existing tribes, a mechanism to ensure fairness of reservations within 
these six communities and related security considerations. The Committee submitted its report 
on 28.12.2018, which is classified as ‘Secret’.

The State wise receipt of ethanol by OMCs is given in Annexure A. 
(b): The Government has advised the OMCs to blend 10% ethanol in petrol. The 
ethanol blended petrol percentage has progressively increased from 1.53% in ESY 2013-
14 (December 2013 to November 2014) to 5% in ESY 2019-20. For ESY 2020-21 the 
Public Sector OMCs have allocated 325.5 crore litres of ethanol upto 01.03.2021 against 
requirement of 457 Crore litres for ESY 2020-21. 
Under the EBP Programme, Government has initiated several interventions both on the 
supply and demand side. The important initiatives are:  reintroduction of administered 
price mechanism for ethanol procurement, enhancement of scope of raw material by 
allowing ethanol production from multiple feed-stocks like C & B heavy molasses, 
sugarcane juice, sugar, sugar syrup, damaged food grains, maize and surplus stocks of 
rice with Food Corporation of India (FCI), differentiated ex-mill price of ethanol to be 
paid to ethanol suppliers based on raw materials used for its production, amendment to 
the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act (IDR Act) – 1951 for free movement of 
ethanol in the country, reduction of  GST rate to 5% on ethanol procured under the EBP 
Programme, formulation of a long term procurement policy for ethanol, interest 
subvention scheme for augmentation and enhancement of ethanol production capacities 
in the country, etc. 
In addition, Public Sector Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) have simplified the ethanol 
procurement procedure thereby encouraging more vendors to take part in the EoIs 
released by them. Due to the above initiatives taken by the Government the ethanol 
procurement has increased from 38 crore litres in ESY 2013-14 to 173.03 crore litre in 
ESY 2019-20. 

(c): OMCs have informed that in the current year they have allocated 325.5 Crore 
litres of ethanol against the requirement of 457 Crore litres ethanol.The source-wise 
breakup of the offers of 325.5croreliters is as under:

This quantity of 325.5 crore litres of ethanol allocated is from 1G ethanol plants only. At

(d): Government has allowed procurement of ethanol produced from other non-food 
feedstock like cellulosic and lingo-cellulosic materials. Government has also launched a 
scheme “Pradhan Mantri JI-VAN (Jaiv Indhan- Vatavaran Anukool fasal awashesh 
Nivaran) Yojana” to provide financial support for promotion of 2G ethanol with a 
financial outlay of Rs.1969.50 crore. 
(e): The properties of the end product viz., ethanol produced from molasses and 
sugarcane are the same. In fact molasses is a byproduct of the sugar-making process, and 
it comes from crushed sugar cane. Government has now also allowed the production of

system and Molecular Sieve Dehydration (MSDH) Column etc. for which interest 
subvention @6% per annum or 50% of the actual rate of interest charged by lending 
institutions whichever is lower on the loans  advanced by  Banks/NCDC/IREDA/NBFCs 
and any other financial institutions. So far a total of Rs. 4687 crore has been earmarked 
towards payment of interest subvention under these schemes.  
The various measures taken by the Government from time to time to increase production 
of ethanol in the country and to promote its supply to OMCs under EBP Programme have 
been provided in the reply of para (b) of this question.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
(MINISTRY OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS) 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. † 2995 
TO BE ANSWERED ON: 15.03.2021 
  
EMPLOYMENT FOR SCHEDULED TRIBES IN SOCIAL SECTOR 
  
†2995.      SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH PATEL: 
  
Will the Minister of Tribal Affairs be pleased to state:  
(a) the prospects of employment for the Scheduled Tribes in the social sector; 
(b)  whether any new scheme is going to be operated in the aspirational districts; and 
(c)  if so, the time by which the said scheme is likely to be implemented? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
(SMT. RENUKA SINGH SARUTA)   
(a) The Ministry of Tribal Affairs implements various schemes for welfare and 
development of Scheduled Tribes including employment in social sector. The Ministry 
provides funds to the State Governments based on their proposals for undertaking various 
employment generation activities including agriculture, horticulture, animal husbandry, 
fisheries and other non-farmbased livelihood activities etc. and Skill & entrepreneurship 
development under the schemes ‘Special Central Assistance to Tribal Sub-Scheme (SCA 
to TSS)’, ‘Development of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs)’, ‘Minimum 
Support Price for Minor Forest Produce (MSP for MFP)’ and ‘Grants under Article 275(1)’. 
The details of State-wise funds release during 2020-21 under the major schemes of 
Ministry is as per Annexure 1. 
The Ministry of Tribal Affairs is also implementing a scheme 'Institutional Support for 
development and marketing of Tribal Product/Produce' wherein Grants-in-aid are provided 
to State Tribal Development Cooperative Corporations (STDCCs) and Tribal Cooperative 
Marketing Development Federation of India Ltd. (TRIFED). The objective of the scheme 
is to create institutions to support marketing and development of tribal products, 
including training and skill up-gradation of tribal Artisans, Craftsmen, MFP gatherers 
and creation of supply chain infrastructure etc. Under the scheme, TRIFED provides 
marketing platform for tribal products through its network of 73 Tribes India outlets and 33 
consignment counters and 15 Franchise outlets in State Emporiums located across the 
country along with other e-commerce platforms. TRIFED also organizes National Tribal 
Festival “Aadi Mahotsav" for development of traditional art and culture of tribal population 
which includes food and handicraft items. The funds released under the scheme during 
last three financial years are as under: 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 
(Amount in lakh rupees) 
Scheme 2017-18 2018-19 2019-20 
Institutional Support 4495.00 7250.00 12850.00 
 
Under the scheme of Minimum Support Price for Minor Forest Produce (MSP for MFP), 
TRIFED also implements the initiative of Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVKs), launched in 
2018-19, wherein tribal community owned Minor Forest Produce centric multi-purpose 
Kendras are set up in predominantly tribal districts which act as common facility centres 
for procurement cum value addition to locally available MFPs. State-wise list of VDVKs 
sanctioned by TRIFED and the number of beneficiaries engaged in MFP value chain 
development activities is at Annexure 2. 
Besides, National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation (NSTFDC), 
under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs extends concessional loans to the eligible Scheduled 
Tribe persons for undertaking any income generation activities/ self-employment through 
its implementing agencies under its schemes namely Term Loan, Adivasi Mahila 
Sashaktikaran Yojana, Micro Credit Scheme for Self Help Groups. The details of amount 
sanctioned, number of beneficiaries covered against said sanctions, amount disbursed 
and number of beneficiaries assisted covered under each of the Schemes of NSTFDC 
during the last three years is given as Annexure 3. 
(b) & (c) No such proposal is under consideration in the Ministry.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2997 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 15.03.2021 
 
INTERNAL MIGRATION IN INDIA 
 
2997. SHRIMATI APARAJITA SARANGI: 
  
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)whether the Government maintains the data of the number of persons 
who have migrated externally from each state in India to another in the 
last 10 years;  
(b)if so, the details thereof specific to external migration from Odisha in 
the last 10 years, including the reasons for the same; 
(c)if not, whether the Government has plans to conduct surveys to assess 
the same and if so, details thereof and if not, the reasons therefore;  
(d)whether the Government plans to release “Migration in India” reports 
for the years subsequent to 2008 and if so, details thereof and if not, 
the reasons therefore; 
(e)whether the Government considers updating the data more frequently 
given the increasing trend in internal migration within India and if so, 
the details thereof and the action taken thereon; and 
(f)if not, the reasons therefore? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE (IC) FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SHRI SANTOSH KUMAR GANGWAR) 
 
(a) to (f): Migration of workers from one place to another  is a 
continuous process. The workers migrate out of their native places in 
search of livelihood. The Constitution of India guarantees the right to 
every citizen to move and reside in any State/UT in search of 
Occupation/Job. According to the Economic S urvey 2016-17 the size of 
the workforce as per Ce nsus 2011, was 482 million (48.2 crore) people 
and based on extrapolation, this figure could have exceeded 500 million 
(50 crore) in 2016. If the share of migrants in the workforce is estimated 
to be even 20%, the size of the migrant workforce can be estim ated to 
be over 100 million (10 crore) in 2016 in absolute terms. 
Contd..2/- 
 

:: 2 :: 
 
Labour Bureau, an attached office of the Ministry of Labour & 
Employment , has been entrusted with the task of conducting the All India 
Survey on Migrant workers.  
 
Ministry of Labour & Employment is developing                        
a comprehensive National Data base of the Unorganized workers (NDUW) 
to collect relevant information of unorganized workers and inter -alia help 
in delivery of various social security and welf are schemes being 
implemented for them. 
 
Further, Ministry of Statistical and Programme  Implementation., 
National Statistical Office (NSO) launched Multiple Indicator Survey 
during January - December 2020.  In this survey, provisions have been 
made to capture information on migration. The information is being 
collected on last usual place of residence of the migrants in relation to 
the place where they are being listed (present place of enumeration)  in 
terms of the following details: 
 
(i) rural area of same district 
(ii) urban area of same district  
(iii) rural area of same state but another district 
(iv) urban area of same state but another district  
(v) rural area of  another state 
(vi) urban area of  another state  
(vii) another country 
 
Besides, as part of the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) of 
National Statistical Office (NSO) information is being collected durin g 
July 2020 – June 2021 on  (i) migration and (ii) temporary visitors in the 
selected households.
